text:
TREC 2025 provides a useful diagnostic taxonomy: distinguish functional substitutes from complements, then distinguish compatible, incompatible, and unknown compatibility. It explicitly separates insufficient evidence from known incompatibility and includes “unable to assess” relatedness. These are product relationships, not evidence that a user needs another item. [Task and annotation definitions](https://trec-product-search.github.io/recommendations.html). For extracting specifications, WDC-PAVE (2024) evaluates attribute extraction and normalization from titles/descriptions against manually verified labels; a 2026 preprint highlights how normalization rules and annotation noise can substantially affect reported extraction quality. [WDC-PAVE](https://arxiv.org/abs/2403.02130), [evaluation audit](https://arxiv.org/abs/2607.22949).

Suggested adaptation: construct matched catalog pairs differing in one documented attribute—connector, model generation, dimensions, media format—while retaining item IDs, evidence spans, normalized values, and labeling rules. Label each specific compatibility/relevance claim supported, contradicted, or unknown; missing specifications remain unknown. This extends the contrast-set principle of small, meaningful changes and evidence-attribution work that evaluates whether claims have adequate support. [Contrast sets](https://arxiv.org/abs/2004.02709), [Attribute or Abstain, 2024](https://aclanthology.org/2024.emnlp-main.463/). Treat textual similarity as a redundancy candidate, not proof of a fulfilled need; interaction history establishes neither ownership nor satisfaction.

For the twenty users, audit only feedback that explicitly addresses each probe claim. Report evidence coverage, feedback coverage, unknown rate, agreement/disagreement counts and denominators, per category and user; inspect disagreements individually. For selective labeling, report error among supported/contradicted decisions alongside decision coverage, preventing abstention from hiding errors. No feedback was supplied here, so these are proposed diagnostics, not measured findings; infer no simulator traits and retain macro validation HR@10 for model selection.
